calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a detached house, a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to those detached-house lot requirements (despite 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)). Keyed PROCEDURAL: it governs how exception lot requirements map onto the houseplex, with no value of its own.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content; the 'only residential building on a lot' condition has no vocabulary token.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a semi-detached house, a semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to the exception's lot requirements for the portion of a semi-detached house that is one dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content; the 'only residential building on a lot' condition has no vocabulary token.

calculation_handling.description: For a detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex or residential building with a secondary suite, if the base lot coverage under 10.40.30.40 is more permissive than the coverage carried in from a Chapter 900 exception under 10.40.30.1(1), the more permissive (base) coverage prevails. Ranked base > exception for lot coverage only.
calculation_handling.gaps: The ranking is limited to lot coverage and to the listed building types.

10.40.30.1(1).explanation: If a site-specific exception (Chapter 900) sets lot requirements for a detached or semi-detached house, the same requirements apply to a detached or semi-detached houseplex that is the only home building on the lot.

10.40.30.1(2).explanation: For a houseplex or a house with a secondary suite, if the regular RS lot coverage rule is more generous than the coverage from a site-specific exception, the more generous rule applies.
